title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 231 (Power of Tribunal to enforce compromise or arrangement)

content.overview: Section 231 empowers the Tribunal to supervise the carrying out of a compromise or arrangement sanctioned under section 230, to give directions for its implementation, to modify the order if necessary for proper working, and, if satisfied that the compromise or arrangement cannot be worked satisfactorily, to order winding up of the company. The power is supervisory: it does not allow the Tribunal to rewrite a scheme that was never approved by the statutory majority. Sanction itself remains under sections 230 and 232.
content.glance: Tribunal supervises sanctioned scheme; may give directions or modify for proper working; may order winding up if scheme cannot be worked satisfactorily; supervisory, not a re-sanction power.
content.study: Where the Tribunal makes an order under section 230 sanctioning a compromise or arrangement, it shall have power to supervise the carrying out of the compromise or arrangement and may give such directions or make such modifications as it considers necessary for the proper working. If the Tribunal is satisfied that a compromise or arrangement sanctioned under section 230 cannot be worked satisfactorily with or without modifications, it may order the winding up of the company. Current-law framing: confirm a sanctioned scheme under s. 230; identify implementation difficulties; seek directions or modifications for proper working; only if the scheme cannot be worked satisfactorily, seek winding up. Do not treat s. 231 as a fresh sanction of an unapproved bargain.

sections.heading: Supervision
sections.body: Tribunal has power to supervise carrying out of a compromise or arrangement sanctioned under s. 230.

sections.heading: Directions and Modification
sections.body: May give directions or make modifications necessary for the proper working of the scheme.

sections.heading: Winding Up
sections.body: If satisfied the scheme cannot be worked satisfactorily (with or without modifications), Tribunal may order winding up.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.body: Supervisory only; does not rewrite an unapproved commercial bargain; sanction remains under ss. 230/232.

provisions.title: Power of Tribunal to enforce compromise or arrangement

examples.title: Directions for implementation
examples.body: A sanctioned scheme under s. 230 stalls because a transfer of assets is blocked by a third-party consent. Parties apply under s. 231 for directions to implement the scheme properly.

examples.title: Scheme cannot be worked
examples.body: Despite modifications, the sanctioned arrangement cannot be implemented. The Tribunal, satisfied under s. 231, may order winding up of the company.

hypotheticals.question: May the Tribunal under s. 231 replace the scheme with entirely different commercial terms never voted on?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 231 is supervisory of a scheme already sanctioned under s. 230. Modifications are for proper working of that scheme. It is not a power to impose a new bargain that lacked the statutory majority.

distinctions.title: Enforcement/supervision (s. 231) vs sanction of scheme (s. 230)
distinctions.left: Supervise, direct, modify for working, or wind up if unworkable
distinctions.right: Order meeting and sanction compromise/arrangement on statutory majority

misconceptions.trap: Section 231 lets the Tribunal approve a scheme that never obtained the three-fourths value majority.
misconceptions.correction: Sanction is under s. 230 (and s. 232 for mergers). Section 231 supervises and enforces a scheme already sanctioned; it does not replace the majority requirement.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 231 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm sanctioned scheme under s. 230. II. Identify implementation issue. III. Seek directions/modification or, if unworkable, winding up. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Sanction status; working difficulty; directions sought; precise relief.

examTips: Directions and modifications for proper working.
Winding up only if scheme cannot be worked.

learningObjectives: State the Tribunal’s enforcement powers under s. 231.
enhancement.definition: Section 231 empowers the Tribunal to supervise a sanctioned compromise or arrangement, give directions or modifications for proper working, and order winding up if the scheme cannot be worked satisfactorily.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Once sanctioned, a scheme is under the Tribunal’s supervisory jurisdiction so that implementation difficulties can be resolved or, if unworkable, the company wound up.
essentialIngredients: Winding up if cannot be worked satisfactorily
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 231 is the post-sanction enforcement and supervision rule.
enhancement.problemApplication: Confirm sanction; seek directions or winding up as facts require.
